answer.rationale: Current state: p99 latency 5x target on write path, security patch cannot be reverted, peak settlement traffic. Rollback is ruled out by compliance. Capacity provisioning is slow for immediate relief. Circuit breakers help contain failures but don't resolve the underlying latency problem. Regional failover (memory_b2) has proven effective for latency recovery in degradation scenarios and can shift load away from the primary during peak write conditions. Read replica routing (memory_b5) addresses query load but won't relieve transactional write path pressure during settlement peak. Failover is the highest-confidence lever that both addresses sustained latency and preserves write availability without reverting the mandatory security patch. Verifying memory_b2 (failover success pattern) and memory_b5 (read-only vs write path distinction) to confirm the technical fit before committing.
